tasks.spec:
You are fixing ONE defect in a Python module's bio extraction: the word-count ceiling throws away real professional bios. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY THREE FILES:
  1. server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py   (edit)
  2. tests/test_guest_email_context.py        (edit — extend, do not delete existing tests)
  3. fix-summary.md                           (create)

Touching any other file fails the check. Do NOT edit server/pipeline/guest_assets.py.

## Why this matters

On 2026-08-11, minutes after round r32 landed (third-person bios accepted, Outlook history stripped, boilerplate rejected), a live run against a real guest's mailbox showed the guest's actual professional bio STILL excluded: it measures 123 words by the module's own _WORD_RE, and gather_guest_email_context only accepts paragraphs of 25..120 words. Every r32 signal fired on that paragraph — third-person name-plus-credentials shape, a "Here's a quick bio" cue paragraph directly above it — and the ceiling discarded it anyway. Professional bios routinely run 120-250 words; the guest even wrote "The sentences are a bit lengthy" above theirs.

## The defect

In gather_guest_email_context (around the paragraph loop, near 'is_bio_signal'), the candidate filter is:

    25 <= word_count <= 120 and is_bio_signal and not _is_bio_boilerplate(...)

is_bio_signal is the OR of three signals introduced by r32: _FIRST_PERSON_RE match, _is_third_person_bio(paragraph, name_tokens), and _BIO_CUE_RE on the previous paragraph. The single 120-word ceiling applies to all three.

## The fix contract

STRONG signals earn a higher ceiling; the WEAK signal keeps the current one; the floor is untouched:

- STRONG: _is_third_person_bio(...) is true, OR the previous paragraph matches _BIO_CUE_RE. Accept 25..250 words.
- WEAK: only _FIRST_PERSON_RE matched (first-person pronouns are everywhere in conversational email — 'Let Me Run' fires on 'Me'). Keep 25..120.
- Floor: 25 words for every path, unchanged.
- _is_bio_boilerplate rejection applies unchanged on every path.
- Do not restructure the module; the smallest honest change to the filter wins. Never merge, trim or rewrite guest content beyond the existing whitespace normalisation.

Add tests to tests/test_guest_email_context.py: a >120-word third-person bio with a cue paragraph is accepted; the same bio without the cue is accepted; a >120-word first-person conversational paragraph (no name shape, no cue) is still rejected; a <25-word paragraph is still rejected. Build long fixtures so their _WORD_RE count is provably in band — count them in the test (assert 120 < count <= 250) so the fixture cannot drift kinder than production, which is exactly how the r32 fixture missed this defect.

Keep every existing test passing. If a pre-r33 test hard-codes the 120 ceiling for a STRONG-signal paragraph, that test encodes this defect: update it to the new contract and say so in your summary; every other existing test must pass unmodified.

## Run ALL THREE until each passes

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_guest_email_context.py tests/test_guest_assets_orchestrator.py tests/test_guest_assets_wiring.py -q
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u21_guest_assets_check.py --worktree "$PWD"
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u25_bio_length_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

u21 is the r32 regression gate — it must STAY green. u25 is this round's defect — it starts red (L1, L2) and must end green without breaking its L3/L4 guards.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of ALL THREE commands. Under 'Risk' name one message shape that could still defeat the extraction after this fix. Under 400 words.
